name: Museum Grünes Haus
kurzbeschreibung: The Museum Grünes Haus in Reutte features striking green trompe-l'œil facade frescoes, baroque Zeiller religious art, and regional Außerfern cultural history.
preis: Adults €6.00, concessions €5.00, children up to 14 free
beschreibung:
Overview

The Museum Grünes Haus (Green House Museum) in the historic market town of Reutte in the Tyrolean Außerfern is recognized as one of the most architecturally distinctive and art-historically significant townhouses in Western Austria. Located on Untermarktstraße, the stately building owes its name to its vivid emerald-green exterior color scheme. The exterior facade itself is an acknowledged masterpiece of baroque illusionistic trompe-l'œil painting: simulated architectural columns, painted window surrounds, and ornamental scrollwork lend the residence the majestic air of a noble palace. As an award-winning regional museum, the Grünes Haus showcases the cultural heritage, artisan traditions, and sacred treasures of the entire district. This unique monument stands as a crown jewel of alpine decorative painting, drawing architecture and history lovers alike.

Route & Requirements

The property dates back to the 16th century, having served prosperous merchants and salt-trade administrators as a grand residential and commercial depot. In 1779, the renowned Reutte baroque master painter Johann Jakob Zeiller created the magnificent illusionistic facade frescoes. Across three modernized exhibition levels, visitors discover a rich collection of cultural treasures. A major exhibition focus is dedicated to the Zeiller artist dynasty, celebrated across Central Europe in the 18th century for their brilliant fresco work in abbeys and churches. Oil paintings, bozzetti, and preparatory sketches illustrate their artistic mastery. Historic tools, documents, and scale models illustrate the arduous daily life and superior craftsmanship of local Außerfern artisans. Additional galleries showcase the medieval history of the Ehrenberg fortress complex, guild items of local masons and plasterers, and sacred decorative arts.

Visit & Arrival

The museum is open Tuesday through Sunday from 13:00 to 17:00 (in July and August opening extended from 10:00; closed Mondays). Admission: adults €6.00, seniors €5.00, children up to 14 free. Discounts apply with the Reutte guest card. By public transport: take the Außerfernbahn railway to Reutte in Tirol station; from there, walk seven minutes through the town center to Untermarkt 24. By car: via the Fernpass road B179 to the Reutte exit; public parking is available in the town center.

Tips

Thanks to a passenger elevator, the museum is fully accessible and wheelchair friendly. Examine the exterior trompe-l'œil murals from various angles before entering to appreciate the optical depth of baroque perspective. Join a guided tour to discover subtle artistic nuances in Zeiller's frescoes. Pair your visit with an excursion to nearby Ehrenberg Castle and the highline179 suspension bridge.
